findings.title: Midnight timestamps silently expand into whole-day bounds
findings.description: Pydantic tries `date` first and converts midnight datetime strings into dates. Verified through the endpoint: `end=2026-06-01T00:00:00Z` reaches the reader as `23:59:59.999999Z`, returning an extra day's data. Midnight timestamps with offsets also lose their offset. Both routes are affected. Preserve the distinction between date-only inputs and timestamps, and add midnight/offset regression tests.

findings.title: Large responses block the event loop
findings.description: Database reads use an executor, but model construction and serialization run synchronously inside the async handler. A local 75,000-candle benchmark measured approximately 708 ms building models plus 550 ms serializing—well beyond the required 1 ms bound, blocking unrelated requests. The trades handler has the same pattern. Offload construction and serialization after releasing the connection; add a concurrent large-response/event-loop-latency test.

findings.title: Load tests are not enforced by CI
findings.description: The new load suite requires manual opt-in, and the inspected CI workflow only publishes tags. Deferring gating to slice 907 does not satisfy the requirement that network/concurrency changes gate on load tests. Add a CI job that runs this tier against a throwaway database for relevant changes.
